To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients with schizophrenia show a blunted response to facial expressions, possibly due to reduced neural sensitivity to irregular faces in the fusiform gyril, possibly mediated by reduced functional connectivity with emotion‐related brain regions.

patients with schizophrenia show reduced sensitivity to irregular facial expressions, which is reflected both in behavioral ratings and in neural sensitivity of the fusiform cortex to repeated presentation of faces.

1) Patients with schizophrenia show less sensitivity to bizarre faces in comparison with controls; 2) This deficiency is reflected by reduced behavioral and neural response to bizarre faces in the FG; and 3) The FG in patients with schizophrenia, compared with controls, shows reduced functional connectivity with emotion‐related regions, the amygdala, and prefrontal regions.
